minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 10, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on November 10, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 5, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

There were no Closed Session agenda items.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present

City Council Minutes  1  November 10, 2015
 INVOCATION: Mayor Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by Senator Patricia Bates on Legislative Updates

  The City Council and audience received the presentation from Senator Pat Bates.

P2.  Presentation on Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball Team Kids Camp 2015

  The City Council and audience received the presentation from Victor Gonzalez.

Presentation on the 240th birthday of the Marine Corps

Mayor Pro Tem Raths shared a video on the 240th birthday of the Marine Corps and he cut a
birthday cake with a fellow veteran from the audience.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mike Hamel, Irvine Chief of Police: stated that Mayor Schlicht's comments at a prior Council
meeting about the Irvine Police Department refusing to take police reports were false and without
merit.

Pat Rizco, James Styles, and Dennis Schwalm, Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 6024, Mission
Viejo: presented the Mayor with a certificate of appreciation for the City's support of active duty
military and veterans and for providing a space at city hall for veterans to come and receive
assistance in preparing disability claims.

Al Holguin, M.V.: stated that he is an atheist, humanist and free thinker and although he and his
wife sit during the pledge of allegiance and religious invocation, it is not a sign of disrespect to
troops and veterans.

Cynthia Cantrelle, Saddleback Republican Assembly (SRA) President, Laguna Woods: stated that
a letter sent to the City Attorney by the SRA on March 16, 2015, listed a post office box that
belongs to her personally. She did not write the letter and she did not authorize use of her personal
post office box. She stated that there are things written in the letter that need to be addressed and
she will investigate and respond back to the City at a future date.

Donna Snow: announced that a letter to the editor appearing in a recent issue of the Community
Common Sense newspaper lists her name as the author but she did not write the article. She stated
that the real author is Connie Lee, a resident of Mission Viejo. Ms. Snow further stated that she
has asked the editor to clear her name in the next issue of the newspaper.

City Council Minutes  2  November 10, 2015
 Rudy Padrol, M.V.: asked the City to support his business, Rudy's Christmas Trees, as he raises
funds for military and veterans’ programs. He also asked the City to refer him to organizations
that may be able to support his efforts.

Elizabeth Busick, M.V.: invited residents to the annual holiday book sale at the Mission Viejo
Library on Monday, November 23, from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Chuck McCollough, M.V.: announced upcoming Chamber of Commerce events including the
monthly mixer and weekly meetings.

Elisa Sierakowski, M.V.: speaking on behalf of her daughter, Valerie Sierakowski, who is working
on her Girl Scouts Gold Award project, she thanked the City for the Community Emergency
Preparedness Academy (CEPA.) She also announced that Valerie is the founder of the website
petprep.org where people can find information on protecting and caring for their pet in the event
of an emergency.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: thanked the Council Members for voting to approve the ITF Wheelchair
Tennis championships and City staff for working so hard to make the event possible. She stated
that the athletes have every right to think of themselves as victims but they don't; they only focus
on what they can do and they do it to the very best of their ability.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Joe Tully, M.V.: speaking about agenda item 10, he discussed the history of the restroom master
plan and expressed support for the construction of a restroom at Pavion Park.

Items 3, 4, and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  3  November 10, 2015
   Approved the minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 27, 2015, as
  presented.

5.  Quarterly Check Register Report – First Quarter of FY 2015-16

  Received and filed.

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo – First Quarter of 2015-16

  Received and filed.

7.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Trabuco to Alicia Parkway - (CIP 221) - Notice
  of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $35,678.21,
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

8.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule

  (1) Adopted Resolution 15-56 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing
  Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications; and (2) adopted Resolution 15-57
  Amending the City’s Authorized Position Schedule for Fiscal Years 2015- 2017.

10.  Pavion Park Restroom Construction - Authorization to Bid - (CIP 304)

  (1) Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Pavion Park Restroom Construction - (CIP 304.)

11.  Request to change the start time for Community Services Commission meetings.

  (1) Approved the Community Services Commission's recommendation to change their
  meeting start time from 6:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., and (2) adopted Resolution 15-58 Changing
  the Established Meeting Time for the Community Services Commission.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated October 16, 2015 in the Amount of $1,175,702.14

City Council Minutes  4  November 10, 2015
   Mayor Schlicht inquired about payments for geotechnical services on Tendaya Street.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that he
  believes it was a street issue but staff will have to get back to her with a full response.

  Referring to a payment for a $24,000 camera, Mayor Schlicht stated that it is not the role
  of government to run a TV station and she would like MVTV to be self-supporting instead
  of taxpayer supported.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated October 23, 2015 in the Amount of $2,242,065.08

  Mayor Schlicht asked about a payment to C&D Electric for the repair of six entry signs
  and $18,000 for an outdoor wireless system. She also expressed concern with plant
  purchases that are made outside of the landscape contracts which include plants. She asked
  if the City is back on a routine park maintenance program and if staff will report back on
  the issue of the performance bond for Merchants Landscape.

  Staff responded to the questions and/or agreed to return with detailed answers at a later
  time.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Bocce Ball Courts at Oso Viejo Community Park- (CIP 324)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht asked questions of staff and expressed concern with bid protests and the
  rejection of the lowest bid.

City Council Minutes  5  November 10, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  award contract to Pacific Tennis Courts, Inc. (A15-59) for the construction of the Bocce
  Ball Courts at Oso Viejo Community Park in an amount not to exceed $174,388.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

12.  Potential Mission Viejo Youth Center Opportunities

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) not
  establish a dedicated youth center; (2) adopt Resolution 15-59 Amending the Fiscal Year
  15-16 Recreation and Community Services Administration Program Budget in the General
  Fund, Appropriating $23,450 to expand the City's Afterschool Enrichment Program
  (including Los Alisos Intermediate School); and (3) direct staff to evaluate the program
  after the first three months but commit to continuing it through the 2016 school year.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

13.  Community Services Funding - Fiscal Year 2015-16

  Community Services Supervisor Leslie Rea-McDonald presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the Community Services Commission’s recommended funding amounts for the
  Community Services Funding Program, fiscal year 2015-16.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  November 10, 2015
 14.  Request for Proposal from the City of Rancho Santa Margarita for Animal Services

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following made comments in favor of providing animal services to the City of Rancho
  Santa Margarita: Sharon Cody, M.V.; Ann Woodson, M.V.; and Robert D. Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1)
  direct staff to respond to the City of Rancho Santa Margarita with a formally written
  response; (2) return to the City Council with the formal submittal for review and
  concurrence prior to sending to the City of Rancho Santa Margarita; and (3) include a
  proposed response for the City of Laguna Hills only if that city is willing to abide by
  Mission Viejo’s operational structure.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to call the
  question

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:43 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:52
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

16.  Consider Canceling the November 24, 2015, City Council Meeting

City Council Minutes  7  November 10, 2015
   City Manager Wilberg announced that the agenda is projected to be very light for the next
  meeting and Thanksgiving is that week. He stated that the forecasted items can be rolled
  over to the December meeting if the Council wishes to cancel the November 24 meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to cancel
  the November 24, 2015, City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Muirlands Boulevard Slopes and Right-of-Way Landscape

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to hold on
  this topic and come back at another time after the drought and El Nino storms have passed.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including an Orange County
Taxpayers Association meeting on taxation in Orange County, a band competition at Mission
Viejo High School, the Wheelchair Doubles Masters tournament, Diane Harkey’s State Board of
Equalization “Connecting Women to Power” conference, and a SCAG meeting in Los
Angeles. She asked staff to schedule a presentation at an upcoming Council Meeting for a report
on recent activities at SCAG. Council Member Bucknum thanked the Orange County Register for
three recent articles on the Wheelchair Tennis Masters, a resident veteran and La Paz Elementary
school. She also discussed a Building Industry Association (BIA) program on smart streets and
she asked staff to look at the concept of changing the paint at intersections to help bicyclists
City Council Minutes  8  November 10, 2015
 navigate through them, to see if that would be a good fit for Mission Viejo. Council Member
Bucknum noted that the City received a letter from the Orange County Mosquito and Vector
Control District asking that Dave Leckness be reappointed to the OCMVC Board of Directors. She
reminded residents that there will be a holiday toy drive for the City’s adopted Marine Battalion
families. She encouraged residents to drop a toy or two in the bins which will be located at all of
the main city facilities and she said there is also a shoe box program for the Marines. Council
Member Bucknum mentioned that tomorrow’s Veterans Day observance will be held at 2:00 p.m.
at the Murray Community and Senior Center and lastly, she encouraged residents to visit the City’s
website to find out more about the many holiday activates in town.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs congratulated and thanked the Orange County Sheriff’s Department for
their quick capture of the bandits that robbed a jewelry store at the Shops at Mission Viejo. Mr.
Sachs noted that he wrote to and personally thanked Senator Pat Bates for her work on AB
1217. He recognized that Assembly Member Brough and Senator Moorlach also worked very
hard to see that AB 1217 is now a two-year bill and hopefully it will be defeated if it comes up
again next year. Council Member Sachs announced that 2012 and 2014 City Council candidate,
Desi Kiss, recently passed away. He stated that he will remember Desi and his activism and desire
to see that the City become even better than it currently is. Council Member Sachs asked that the
meeting be dedicated to Desi.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury had no comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths echoed Council Member Sachs’ comments regarding Desi Kiss. He stated
that he worked with Desi during the last campaign and he expressed his sympathy to Mr. Kiss’
wife and family. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he is looking forward to the Veterans Day
ceremony tomorrow at 2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. He also expressed concern
with the Community Common Sense newspaper and the fact that they’re publishing articles under
fake names. He stated that regular newspapers do not do that nor would they publish an opinion
piece and withhold the name of the author. He asked the editors of the newspaper to look into the
claims that they are using fake names. Mayor Pro Tem Raths then read a prepared statement
regarding the two ladies who came forward to denounce recent activities at the Saddleback
Republican Assembly (SRA) and missing monies that were supposed to go to the SRA Treasury
but instead went to fund the Community Common Sense newspaper. He asserted that resident
Connie Lee is behind the missing money and he asked her to come forward. Mayor Pro Tem Raths
discussed his disappointment with Mayor Schlicht’s term as Mayor. He questioned her suitability
to continue, stating that she does not serve the best interests of the citizens of Mission Viejo and
therefore he requested that she resign as Mayor immediately.

City Council Minutes  9  November 10, 2015
 Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that Mayor Pro Tem Raths’ comments have everything to do with the
November 2016 election. She asked staff if there is any truth to the rumors that the former Haggen
grocery store property may be rezoned for residential and City Manager Wilberg stated that he is
not aware of that. Mayor Schlicht asked staff if they received her concerns about trenching that
damaged tree roots and she thanked Council Member Ury for his forward-thinking assessment in
getting the City prepared for El Nino. She asked if the recent rains brought any downed trees and
Director Rattay said there were very few fallen trees. Mayor Schlicht asked if staff should consider
increasing the number of sand bags available to residents and Director Rattay responded that the
supply is re-stocked as needed. She also encouraged homeowners to consider purchasing flood
insurance as she and her family have done. Mayor Schlicht thanked Senator Pat Bates for her
insightful observation and visions on how to govern from a minority seat and she stated that we
all owe the Senator a debt of thanks for her hard work. She also thanked Mr. and Mrs. Victor
Gonzalez for seeing a need in the community and making a difference. Mayor Schlicht outlined
her attendance at the South Orange County Association of Mayors meeting with guest speaker Ron
Kingston, a leading expert on PACE loan risks. She mentioned a Wall Street Journal article on
the topic and she asked the City Attorney to share it with the other Council Members. She also
attended the City Selection Committee meeting where Frank Ury was reappointed to the OCTA
Board and where she voted for Dwight Robinson for the Air Quality Management District
(AQMD) Board. She stated that the latter was a contested race and Mr. Robinson’s appointment
switched the majority from Democrat to Republican. She also discussed her attendance at the
City-hosted Wheelchair Tennis Masters where she gave out some awards to the finalists. She
commented that she didn’t even notice the wheelchairs, she just noticed the level of play and that
the professional athletes demonstrate that all is possible. Mayor Schlicht announced that she will
close the meeting in memory of Desi Kiss. At his funeral service, it was apparent that Desi’s main
attribute was his integrity. She noted that Mr. Kiss received 5,798 votes in the last election which
was pretty good for a grass-roots effort. And in closing, Mayor Schlicht thanked our country’s
peace keepers for their service and sacrifice and she shared a quote from Daniel Webster in honor
of Veterans Day: “God grants liberty only to those who love it, and are always ready to guard and
defend it.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:36 p.m. with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting, in memory of Desi Joseph Kiss, to Tuesday, December 8,
2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 8, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  November 10, 2015
